messages:
Bob (ACME): Hey, team — after the scale-up yesterday our assistant stopped honoring the anchored system instruction in long sessions. We used to get numbered steps every time, now it returns freeform prose mid-conversation.

Ellie (Support): Sorry about that. Can you paste a minimal repro (API call + conversation) and which model / region you hit? Any request IDs or response headers?

Bob (ACME): Model: redwood-instruct-4k (hosted, us-west-2). Repro below — long multi-turn history (~10 user/assistant turns) + system prompt at the top: "You are a helpful assistant. Always answer in numbered steps." The assistant returns unnumbered paragraphs. Example request we sent:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-4k","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant. Always answer in numbered steps."},{"role":"user","content":"We have a deployment checklist for onboarding. Give me the steps to onboard a new user who needs SSO + billing."},{"role":"assistant","content":"(older reply)\n1. Create user\n2. ..."},{"role":"user","content":"Now summarize the items and next actions."}]}'
```

Bob (ACME): Expected: reply with numbered steps (because system prompt anchors format). Actual response we received:

"Here are the things you need to do: set up SSO, configure billing, invite the user. Keep an eye on quotas."

No numbers, no explicit steps. This only happens when the conversation is long — short sessions still obey the system prompt.

Ellie (Support): Did you see any error codes or context-truncation warnings in headers? Any spikes in latency?

Bob (ACME): We had one 503 around the same time and a couple of slow responses. Example response headers from the failing request: "x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d", "x-runtime-ms: 3520", and our app logs show "context_truncated=true" for that request. No billing or auth issues.

Jamal (Eng Oncall): Thanks, looping in eng. @Ellie can you attach the full transcript and the raw request/response payloads (we need the exact tokens sent upstream)? Two quick hypotheses: 1) the scale-up added a compact fallback variant with smaller context and routing may be selecting it for some sessions, truncating the system prefix; 2) KV/prefix caching eviction bug after autoscale that drops earlier system messages for long histories.

Ellie (Support): Attached the transcript and the request_id list to the ticket. Also included approximate token counts (input ~3600 tokens) and the full messages array.

DeployBot: Deployment event: scale-up completed at 2109360000. New pool added: redwood-instruct-4k-compact (config: max_context=3000, lower memory).

Jamal (Eng Oncall): That matches suspicion #1 — the compact variant would drop the earliest tokens when token count > 3000, which would evict the system message. We'll check routing logic that matches requests to variants; it should prefer variants meeting the session's context length.

Sara (CSE): From an account side, customers are seeing functional regressions. If this is a routing bug we should prioritize a hotfix or rollback the variant until we validate.

Jamal (Eng Oncall): Agreed. Immediate action: 1) disable compact variant for the host pool, 2) re-run the repro request pinned to the main pool and confirm restores anchored behavior, 3) add telemetry to detect system-prefix eviction. Ellie — can you confirm Bob when we disable the compact variant and run the same request?

Ellie (Support): Will do. Bob, we'll do a quick change and ask you to repro. ETA 10–15m.

Bob (ACME): Thanks. Happy to test. I can run a replay script against the request_ids provided.

(10 minutes later)

Ellie (Support): Disabled compact variant and re-routed traffic. Bob, can you re-run the same curl payload pinned to the main pool (we'll give you a test endpoint)?

Bob (ACME): Re-ran the same request against the test endpoint. Model now returns:

"1. Set up SSO with your IdP.\n2. Configure billing and link payment method.\n3. Invite user and assign roles.\n..."

Bob (ACME): Looks fixed for our repro. No 503s this time and latency ~320ms.

Jamal (Eng Oncall): Good — confirms routing to compact variant was the root cause. We'll roll a quick fix to ensure routing selects variants with sufficient max_context for incoming token_count. Follow-ups: add a server-side guard to reject/route any request whose total_tokens > variant.max_context and never silently drop the system prefix; add metric that counts "system_prefix_evicted".

Sara (CSE): We'll keep the account updated and offer a postmortem.

Ellie (Support): Thanks everyone — marking thread for eng postmortem and customer follow-up. :thumbsup:
